section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section focuses on the findings of a single study (Study X) that explored the relationship between positive body image (body appreciation) and women's sexual functioning in a non-clinical, non-college student population. The study found that higher body appreciation positively predicted sexual function, particularly arousal, satisfaction, and orgasm, but not sexual desire or lubrication. It also concluded that BMI did not moderate the relationship between body appreciation and sexual function, contrasting with findings from clinical weight-loss samples.
